 Principal’s Message 
 Dr. J. Paul Jayakar, M.A., M.Phil., Ph.D., PBDCA., 
 Founded in 1881, by the initiatives of the visionary first principal, Rev. G.T. Washburn, the American College began with only four Christian young men. Since then the institution has grown phenomenally in academic excellence and student enrollment. A pioneer in higher education in this region, the College has dedicated itself to training students to serve God and people. The College continues to attract students by offering courses that are globally relevant and equipping them with in-demand employability skills.

 Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) 
 The American College, since its inception, has been adopting a series of changes in its curriculum matching with the advancements in the various Academic subject areas, and the emerging needs and demands from the society. The global perspective of the college has also been a driving force to provide quality education to its students. Autonomy has provided a platform for each department to have their own departmental objectives leading to the emergence of scholars with interdisciplinary background.
 Intellectual profundity and wider choices characterize liberal arts and science undergraduate education. CBCS allows students to cross the artificial boundaries of varied academic disciplines and enables them to get the insights of several disciplines bringing out the inherent interest and aptitude.
 After two-years of deliberations, our faculty has brought out a version of the choice based credit system that suits the needs and aspirations of the American college community. It is not just a change in the nomenclature but also a paradigm shift in the education practices.
 The following are also some of the other expected outcomes:
 CBCS will develop human resources to suit a wide range of career opportunities
 It will promote inter-departmental cooperation within the college for a better utilization of the existing infrastructure and human resources.
 The students can go beyond institutional boundaries by way of transferring credits across accredited institutions.

</header><div class="kingster-page-title-wrap  kingster-style-medium kingster-left-align" ><div class="kingster-header-transparent-substitute" ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-overlay"  ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-container kingster-container" ><div class="kingster-page-title-content kingster-item-pdlr"  ><h1 class="kingster-page-title"  >Choice Based Credit System (CBCS)</h1></div></div></div>	<div class="kingster-page-wrapper" id="kingster-page-wrapper" ><div class="gdlr-core-page-builder-body clearfix"><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section-container gdlr-core-container clearfix" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column gdlr-core-column-60 gdlr-core-column-first" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column-content-margin gdlr-core-js "   ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column-content clearfix gdlr-core-js "   ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-element" ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item gdlr-core-item-pdlr gdlr-core-item-pdb gdlr-core-left-align"  ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item-content" style="text-transform: none ;"  ><p style="text-align: justify;">The American College, since its inception, has been adopting a series of changes in its curriculum matching with the advancements in the various Academic subject areas, and the emerging needs and demands from the society. The global perspective of the college has also been a driving force to provide quality education to its students. Autonomy has provided a platform for each department to have their own departmental objectives leading to the emergence of scholars with interdisciplinary background.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Intellectual profundity and wider choices characterize liberal arts and science undergraduate education. CBCS allows students to cross the artificial boundaries of varied academic disciplines and enables them to get the insights of several disciplines bringing out the inherent interest and aptitude.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">After two-years of deliberations, our faculty has brought out a version of the choice based credit system that suits the needs and aspirations of the American college community. It is not just a change in the nomenclature but also a paradigm shift in the education practices.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The following are also some of the other expected outcomes:</p>
<ul style="text-align: justify;">
<li>CBCS will develop human resources to suit a wide range of career opportunities</li>
<li>It will promote inter-departmental cooperation within the college for a better utilization of the existing infrastructure and human resources.</li>
<li>The students can go beyond institutional boundaries by way of transferring credits across accredited institutions.</li>
</ul>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong><a href="https://americancollege.edu.in/amc-storage/2020/03/CBCS-GRID.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Choice Based Credit System (CBCS)- List of Courses</a></strong></p>

 RESEARCH POLICY AND PRACTICE 
 Policy: 
 Being a college with a difference since its inception in 1881, the American College, Madurai has been an academia par excellence in serving the cause of Higher Education imbued with a holistic perspective in imparting the state-of-the-art knowledge and skills with high seriousness and robustness relevant to contemporary times. Pedagogy of the Twenty First Century – updated and innovative- with a right blend of cutting-edge research has been the hallmark of the college. Fair subscription to original ideas, and framing curriculum adopting novel strategies, improvisations in Teaching- Learning process and evaluation patterns for an effective pedagogy and knowledge-generation/transmission through village outreach programmes, extension projects and  competency- building workshops through the munificent grants offered by the Research and Development Committee of the college have always accelerated the growth of the institution.
 In tune with the recommendations of the Kothari commission on National Policy on Education (1968), the college had championed the cause of Higher Education with three cardinal principles of Excellence, Relevance and Employability . Catering to the needs of the students through enhanced teacher- responsibility coupled with teaching-learning strategies in the stated domains, the college has always addressed the needs and priorities of its stakeholders through consultations and perfect professional expertise at various levels. The spirit of inquiry and conscientious subscription to fair functioning have led to the active research slant in all these approaches. The erstwhile office of the Academic Dean and an exclusive office of Dean for Curriculum Development and Research later, with the advice of the Research and Development committee, have been engaged in monitoring and encouraging the progress of research of the faculty and students.
 In this post-second cycle of NAAC, research policies were revamped and newer references were created to strengthen the domain-centered approach. This in turn, has enhanced infrastructure and research equipment of the departments many fold. The college has made a paradigm shift in creating common instrumentation facilities that offer channels for pursuing innovations and improvisations so as to create a fresh ambience and eco systems for multi-disciplinary and cross-major learning and research. Today, as an integral part of the curriculum, the college promotes independent and group investigations and dissertation studies among undergraduate and postgraduate students. It also encourages its faculty to handle projects that would act as catalysts for developing grant proposals to attract funding agencies in India and abroad.
 Positioned on firm foundation and backed by a century-old experience, the research policy of the college articulates that quality research, which engenders a sound knowledge-based society, is the hallmark of learning in the portal of Higher Education in India. Through effective and innovative measures, the research facility available in the college will direct, augment and invigorate a spirit of enquiry, scientific temperament, research aptitude, capacity-building, and character-formation in grooming researchers. These ideals are well envisioned and nurtured by the object of the institution.
 Practice: 
 Induction and duties of Research scholars: 
 Interested scholars shall apply to the respective universities to clear the eligibility test conducted in July and February.
 Scholars shall apply for research position exist in the college and appear for counseling at the beginning of the academic calendar and the provisional order of admission will be issued by the Principal
 Scholars shall meet the Dean of Research and the original certificates will be submitted in the office.
 On completion of formalities the scholar will be issued a Roll No like 20 PHD **, 20 PHD MAT ** and an ID card which shall be worn by the scholar inside the premises
 An orientation program will be arranged for the newly enrolled scholars.
 A separate attendance register to be maintained at Principals office for all the scholars
 Leave applications to be submitted to the principal’s office forwarded by the Guide on a regular basis
 On-duty leave shall be availed on outside works/conferences /workshops etc.
 Maternity leave is allowed as per UGC norms.
 A Research Advisory Committee for each Department (RAC) is to be formed and the same will finalize the study design and methodology of the research to be done.
 RAC shall comprise: Principal, Dean of research, Heads, Research Guides of the department. (Optional – Two technical experts may be added to the committee for reviewing the progress of the scholars)
 Subsequently scholar will be assigned a mentor for selecting a research TOPIC/GUIDE
 Eligible scholars will be paid a scholarship each month as decided by the administration.
 Scholars shall pay a nominal fee every year for the college and also the University as per requirements.
 Should complete the course work in the first semester. As per MKU rules COE will conduct examinations in regard to the course works.
 The course works shall have 2/4 different courses as prescribed by MKU in the circular no. MKU/PhD/CW2016/Circular-AC to earn 12/14 credits.

</header><div class="kingster-page-title-wrap  kingster-style-small kingster-left-align" style="background-image: url(https://americancollege.edu.in/amc-storage/2021/02/COLLEGE-TOP-VIEW.jpg) ;" ><div class="kingster-header-transparent-substitute" ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-overlay"  ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-bottom-gradient" ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-container kingster-container" ><div class="kingster-page-title-content kingster-item-pdlr"  ><h1 class="kingster-page-title" style="color: #ffffff ;"  >RESEARCH POLICY AND PRACTICE</h1></div></div></div>	<div class="kingster-page-wrapper" id="kingster-page-wrapper" ><div class="gdlr-core-page-builder-body clearfix"><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section-container gdlr-core-container clearfix" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-element" ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item gdlr-core-item-pdlr gdlr-core-item-pdb gdlr-core-left-align"  ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item-content" style="text-transform: none ;"  ><h3><strong><u>Policy:</u></strong></h3>
<p>Being a college with a difference since its inception in 1881, the American College, Madurai has been an academia par excellence in serving the cause of Higher Education imbued with a holistic perspective in imparting the state-of-the-art knowledge and skills with high seriousness and robustness relevant to contemporary times. Pedagogy of the Twenty First Century – updated and innovative- with a right blend of cutting-edge research has been the hallmark of the college. Fair subscription to original ideas, and framing curriculum adopting novel strategies, improvisations in Teaching- Learning process and evaluation patterns for an effective pedagogy and knowledge-generation/transmission through village outreach programmes, extension projects and  competency- building workshops through the munificent grants offered by the Research and Development Committee of the college have always accelerated the growth of the institution.</p>
<p>In tune with the recommendations of the Kothari commission on National Policy on Education (1968), the college had championed the cause of Higher Education with three cardinal principles of <strong>Excellence, Relevance and Employability</strong> . Catering to the needs of the students through enhanced teacher- responsibility coupled with teaching-learning strategies in the stated domains, the college has always addressed the needs and priorities of its stakeholders through consultations and perfect professional expertise at various levels. The spirit of inquiry and conscientious subscription to fair functioning have led to the active research slant in all these approaches. The erstwhile office of the Academic Dean and an exclusive office of <strong>Dean for Curriculum Development and Research</strong> later, with the advice of the Research and Development committee, have been engaged in monitoring and encouraging the progress of research of the faculty and students.</p>
<p>In this post-second cycle of NAAC, research policies were revamped and newer references were created to strengthen the domain-centered approach. This in turn, has enhanced infrastructure and research equipment of the departments many fold. The college has made a paradigm shift in creating common instrumentation facilities that offer channels for pursuing innovations and improvisations so as to create a fresh ambience and eco systems for multi-disciplinary and cross-major learning and research. Today, as an integral part of the curriculum, the college promotes independent and group investigations and dissertation studies among undergraduate and postgraduate students. It also encourages its faculty to handle projects that would act as catalysts for developing grant proposals to attract funding agencies in India and abroad.</p>
<p>Positioned on firm foundation and backed by a century-old experience, the research policy of the college articulates that quality research, which engenders a sound knowledge-based society, is the hallmark of learning in the portal of Higher Education in India. Through effective and innovative measures, the research facility available in the college will direct, augment and invigorate a spirit of enquiry, scientific temperament, research aptitude, capacity-building, and character-formation in grooming researchers. These ideals are well envisioned and nurtured by the object of the institution.</p>
<h3><strong><u>Practice:</u></strong></h3>
<p><strong><u>Induction and duties of Research scholars:</u></strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Interested scholars shall apply to the respective universities to clear the eligibility test conducted in July and February.</li>
<li>Scholars shall apply for research position exist in the college and appear for counseling at the beginning of the academic calendar and the provisional order of admission will be issued by the Principal</li>
<li>Scholars shall meet the Dean of Research and the original certificates will be submitted in the office.</li>
<li>On completion of formalities the scholar will be issued a Roll No like 20 PHD **, 20 PHD MAT ** and an ID card which shall be worn by the scholar inside the premises</li>
<li>An orientation program will be arranged for the newly enrolled scholars.</li>
<li>A separate attendance register to be maintained at Principals office for all the scholars
<ul>
<li>Leave applications to be submitted to the principal’s office forwarded by the Guide on a regular basis</li>
<li>On-duty leave shall be availed on outside works/conferences /workshops etc.</li>
<li>Maternity leave is allowed as per UGC norms.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>A Research Advisory Committee for each Department (RAC) is to be formed and the same will finalize the study design and methodology of the research to be done.</li>
<li>RAC shall comprise: Principal, Dean of research, Heads, Research Guides of the department. (Optional – Two technical experts may be added to the committee for reviewing the progress of the scholars)</li>
<li>Subsequently scholar will be assigned a mentor for selecting a research TOPIC/GUIDE</li>
<li>Eligible scholars will be paid a scholarship each month as decided by the administration.</li>
<li>Scholars shall pay a nominal fee every year for the college and also the University as per requirements.</li>
<li>Should complete the course work in the first semester. As per MKU rules COE will conduct examinations in regard to the course works.</li>
<li>The course works shall have 2/4 different courses as prescribed by MKU in the circular no. MKU/PhD/CW2016/Circular-AC to earn 12/14 credits.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>These courses shall be designed by the Board of studies of the respective department and the same should be presented in the academic council for ratification. Any change in the courses shall be duly effected only after following the usual procedures.</li>
<li>Supplementary examinations will be held in both the odd and even semesters. Scholars who could not complete the course works after two years shall summarily be allowed to exit the program.</li>
<li>Apart from these courses the scholars are encouraged to pass one specialized course conducted by NPTEL or COURSERA or any course equivalent</li>
<li>Grades in the course work shall be finalized by research advisory committee (RAC) and the same will be sent to University.</li>
<li>Mark statement will be issued by the controller of examinations and a course work completion certificate shall be issued by the Dean of Research.</li>
<li>It is mandatory to have the course work mark statement to confirm the provisional PhD registration in the respective Universities and also for the final submission of thesis.</li>
<li>Every year one RAC meeting will be held in April to review the progress of the scholar the committee will authorize in consent with the guide for furthering the research work. Any issues will be sorted here and will be implemented in the following year.</li>
<li>A report of the meeting shall be submitted by committee to the dean office for documentation.</li>
<li>Student will carry out research work independently in the supervision of the GUIDE either in the premises or outside with prior approval from the RAC and Principal.</li>
<li>Scholars will be advised to apply for scholarship from both national and International agencies.</li>
<li>Scholars will be advised to avail Senior Research Fellowship at the end of the second year of research.</li>
<li>Students shall publish at least TWO peer reviewed research papers published in UGC indexed journals before the submission of Ph.D thesis.</li>
<li>Relieving of research scholars shall follow the procedure outline below:</li>
<li>No dues from the guide, department, department library, DPM library, Hostel, Instrumentation centre(for science students) should be obtained</li>
<li>Dean will forward the application to the principal</li>
<li>Principal will formally relieve the student from the college and will order the dean to issue all the certificates.</li>
<li>A research experience certificate will be issued and certified by the Guide, Dean and the Principal & Secretary.</li>
</ul>
<p><code></code></p>
<h3><strong><u>Research Guides:</u></strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Potential research guides should be identified in all streams of Aided/SF/Management programs and should be encouraged to do quality research at the college premises.</li>
<li>The guides will be encouraged to obtain guideship from various UGC recognized research institutions and International institutions.</li>
<li>The guides will be given adequate facilities and can avail the resources in the college premises.</li>
<li>They shall avail on-duty-leave as per government rules and the same can be extended for SF/Management faculties.</li>
<li>Any research guide who is an “outsider” but is willing to use the institution as the research centre will collaborate with any of the faculty of the local department. (An “outsider” is a one who is not a regular member or a faculty of The American College but an expert who is willing to help the students to do their research in their institution or in the college premises)</li>
<li>Guides should keep the record of students of the past and present and should be able to give any information when asked.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong><u>Publication ethics:</u></strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Research guides who encourage scholars to publish in any of the fake journals, predatory journals, fake conferences and fake awards will not be allowed to continue as research guides in the departments.</li>
<li>Scholars should be discouraged to publish papers in paid journals and open journals.</li>
<li>Should engage only Scopus indexed or UGC regulated journals.</li>
<li>Attending Conferences by organizations and associations and local colleges should be discouraged while conferences by Universities and central institutes are encouraged.</li>
<li>Publication and presentation of any form of research shall be done in prior consent from the supervisor.</li>
<li>All publications should carry the guide as the corresponding author.</li>
<li>Scholars who will engage in any of the collaborative work shall get the consent from the guide and any deviation from this practice will invite disciplinary action against the scholar.</li>
<li>The collaborations and MOUs can be signed by the respective guide and the same should be properly intimated to the Deans office and the Principal & Secretary. Any deviations from this practice will invite disciplinary action against the scholar/guide.</li>
<li>Works under collaborations are encouraged while the publications will carry the guides as one of the corresponding author.</li>
<li>Any other practice will not give credentials to scholar and guide and the same is considered as “outsourcing” which is categorically discouraged.</li>
<li>Such publications will not be added to the scholar/guide’s credentials in the college.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong><u>Repository and documentation:</u></strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Guideship orders from guides will be kept in the repository at the Deans office.</li>
<li>All admission letters and scholars related documents and certificates will be kept at the Deans office</li>
<li>The documents related to their guideship, attending conferences/workshops, and peer reviewed publications shall be submitted to the Dean’s office periodically for NAAC/IQAC/NIRF documentation.</li>
<li>The copy of the documents related to any publication should be kept in the respective department and Head will keep a repository of these documents.</li>
<li>Published papers in the reviewed journals and conferences shall be kept at a repository of DPM library and the same will be kept as bound volumes for each year.</li>
<li>The final thesis in the bound form and a soft copy will be kept at the repository of DPM library for public use and reference.</li>
<li>The final thesis should also be submitted to the respective department library for the students use and reference.</li>
<li>College websites will carry the publication records of the year by all the departments and the same should be maintained by the DPM library.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong><u>Change of Guide and Topic:</u></strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>A proposal shall be given by the scholar to the Dean and the same will be analysed by the ARC. The findings shall be forwarded to the principal and upon the Principals approval the same will be forwarded to the respective University for further actions.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong><u>Research Departments:</u></strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>All departments from Aided/SF schemes will be encouraged to receive the recognition from MKU as research centres.</li>
<li>Departments shall keep a record of research guides and students and a notice board shall be kept in regard to this.</li>
<li>A separate research scholar room should be kept in every department.</li>
<li>A scholar will assist the Head to maintain the webpage of research activities of the department showing publications and other research activities.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong><u>Grievance and counseling:</u></strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Any complaint against the scholar can be lodged by the guide directly to Principal and Secretary.</li>
<li>Any complaint against the guide can be lodged by the scholar directly to Principal and Secretary.</li>
<li>Any complaint by the scholar against a fellow scholar or other faculty or staffs can be submitted to the Head of the department or to the Deans office.</li>
<li>Any grievance by women scholars shall approach Dean of Women students, Women’s Hostel wardens and the Dean’s office.</li>
<li>Complaints regarding the academic practices shall be conveyed to the Dean’s office.</li>
<li>Complaints of very serious offences shall be informed directly to the Principal and Secretary.</li>
<li>Committees / ARC or any other Discipline committee shall be formed by the Principal & Secretary in consultation with the Dean and the committee will deal with the complaints raised.</li>
<li>Action on discipline proceedings shall be executed by the Principal & Secretary.</li>
<li>Counseling will be done to complainants and the issues will be resolved within the regulations of the institution.</li>
<li>Taking the allegations and complaints outside the college jurisdiction without the consent from the Principal & Secretary will summarily invite removal of the complainants from the Institution.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong><u>Discipline of scholars:</u></strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Rules and regulations of the college should be adhered</li>
<li>Discipline of scholars shall be maintained as per the college regulations.</li>
</ul>

lists: SLP – CHILD SUPPORT WORK IN ORPHANAGES
SLP – CHILD SUPPORT WORK IN ORPHANAGES
Interested scholars shall apply to the respective universities to clear the eligibility test conducted in July and February.

Scholars shall apply for research position exist in the college and appear for counseling at the beginning of the academic calendar and the provisional order of admission will be issued by the Principal
Scholars shall meet the Dean of Research and the original certificates will be submitted in the office.
On completion of formalities the scholar will be issued a Roll No like 20 PHD **, 20 PHD MAT ** and an ID card which shall be worn by the scholar inside the premises
An orientation program will be arranged for the newly enrolled scholars.
A separate attendance register to be maintained at Principals office for all the scholars Leave applications to be submitted to the principal’s office forwarded by the Guide on a regular basis
On-duty leave shall be availed on outside works/conferences /workshops etc.
Maternity leave is allowed as per UGC norms.

These courses shall be designed by the Board of studies of the respective department and the same should be presented in the academic council for ratification. Any change in the courses shall be duly effected only after following the usual procedures.
Supplementary examinations will be held in both the odd and even semesters. Scholars who could not complete the course works after two years shall summarily be allowed to exit the program.
Apart from these courses the scholars are encouraged to pass one specialized course conducted by NPTEL or COURSERA or any course equivalent
Grades in the course work shall be finalized by research advisory committee (RAC) and the same will be sent to University.
Mark statement will be issued by the controller of examinations and a course work completion certificate shall be issued by the Dean of Research.
It is mandatory to have the course work mark statement to confirm the provisional PhD registration in the respective Universities and also for the final submission of thesis.

Every year one RAC meeting will be held in April to review the progress of the scholar the committee will authorize in consent with the guide for furthering the research work. Any issues will be sorted here and will be implemented in the following year.
A report of the meeting shall be submitted by committee to the dean office for documentation.
Student will carry out research work independently in the supervision of the GUIDE either in the premises or outside with prior approval from the RAC and Principal.
Scholars will be advised to apply for scholarship from both national and International agencies.
Scholars will be advised to avail Senior Research Fellowship at the end of the second year of research.
Students shall publish at least TWO peer reviewed research papers published in UGC indexed journals before the submission of Ph.D thesis.
Relieving of research scholars shall follow the procedure outline below:
No dues from the guide, department, department library, DPM library, Hostel, Instrumentation centre(for science students) should be obtained
Dean will forward the application to the principal
Principal will formally relieve the student from the college and will order the dean to issue all the certificates.
A research experience certificate will be issued and certified by the Guide, Dean and the Principal & Secretary.
Potential research guides should be identified in all streams of Aided/SF/Management programs and should be encouraged to do quality research at the college premises.
The guides will be encouraged to obtain guideship from various UGC recognized research institutions and International institutions.
The guides will be given adequate facilities and can avail the resources in the college premises.
They shall avail on-duty-leave as per government rules and the same can be extended for SF/Management faculties.

Any research guide who is an “outsider” but is willing to use the institution as the research centre will collaborate with any of the faculty of the local department. (An “outsider” is a one who is not a regular member or a faculty of The American College but an expert who is willing to help the students to do their research in their institution or in the college premises)
Guides should keep the record of students of the past and present and should be able to give any information when asked.

Research guides who encourage scholars to publish in any of the fake journals, predatory journals, fake conferences and fake awards will not be allowed to continue as research guides in the departments.
Scholars should be discouraged to publish papers in paid journals and open journals.
Should engage only Scopus indexed or UGC regulated journals.
Attending Conferences by organizations and associations and local colleges should be discouraged while conferences by Universities and central institutes are encouraged.
Publication and presentation of any form of research shall be done in prior consent from the supervisor.
All publications should carry the guide as the corresponding author.
Scholars who will engage in any of the collaborative work shall get the consent from the guide and any deviation from this practice will invite disciplinary action against the scholar.

The collaborations and MOUs can be signed by the respective guide and the same should be properly intimated to the Deans office and the Principal & Secretary. Any deviations from this practice will invite disciplinary action against the scholar/guide.
Works under collaborations are encouraged while the publications will carry the guides as one of the corresponding author.
Any other practice will not give credentials to scholar and guide and the same is considered as “outsourcing” which is categorically discouraged.
Such publications will not be added to the scholar/guide’s credentials in the college.
Guideship orders from guides will be kept in the repository at the Deans office.
All admission letters and scholars related documents and certificates will be kept at the Deans office
The documents related to their guideship, attending conferences/workshops, and peer reviewed publications shall be submitted to the Dean’s office periodically for NAAC/IQAC/NIRF documentation.
The copy of the documents related to any publication should be kept in the respective department and Head will keep a repository of these documents.
Published papers in the reviewed journals and conferences shall be kept at a repository of DPM library and the same will be kept as bound volumes for each year.
The final thesis in the bound form and a soft copy will be kept at the repository of DPM library for public use and reference.
The final thesis should also be submitted to the respective department library for the students use and reference.
College websites will carry the publication records of the year by all the departments and the same should be maintained by the DPM library.

A proposal shall be given by the scholar to the Dean and the same will be analysed by the ARC. The findings shall be forwarded to the principal and upon the Principals approval the same will be forwarded to the respective University for further actions.
All departments from Aided/SF schemes will be encouraged to receive the recognition from MKU as research centres.
Departments shall keep a record of research guides and students and a notice board shall be kept in regard to this.
A separate research scholar room should be kept in every department.
A scholar will assist the Head to maintain the webpage of research activities of the department showing publications and other research activities.
Any complaint against the scholar can be lodged by the guide directly to Principal and Secretary.
Any complaint against the guide can be lodged by the scholar directly to Principal and Secretary.
Any complaint by the scholar against a fellow scholar or other faculty or staffs can be submitted to the Head of the department or to the Deans office.
Any grievance by women scholars shall approach Dean of Women students, Women’s Hostel wardens and the Dean’s office.
Complaints regarding the academic practices shall be conveyed to the Dean’s office.
Complaints of very serious offences shall be informed directly to the Principal and Secretary.
Committees / ARC or any other Discipline committee shall be formed by the Principal & Secretary in consultation with the Dean and the committee will deal with the complaints raised.
Action on discipline proceedings shall be executed by the Principal & Secretary.
Counseling will be done to complainants and the issues will be resolved within the regulations of the institution.
Taking the allegations and complaints outside the college jurisdiction without the consent from the Principal & Secretary will summarily invite removal of the complainants from the Institution.
Rules and regulations of the college should be adhered
Discipline of scholars shall be maintained as per the college regulations.

 Attendance 
 Attendance will be marked at the beginning of each class.
 Students shall assemble in the respective lecture rooms before the second bell.
 In every class, each student shall have a specified seat and shall not occupy any other seat without the permission of the teacher.
 No student shall absent themselves from the College without obtaining leave except in case of sudden illness or ether circumstances which may prevent them from so doing. The Vice-Principal is the authority for granting leave.
 Application for leave must be written specifying clearly the reasons. They must be countersigned by the Parent or Guardian or Hall Warden before being sent to the Vice-Principal. Sick leave exceeding two days should be supported by a Medical Certificate.
 Students who absent themselves from College without leave shall pay a fine according to the following rule :
  Attendance (%)     
 Fine 
 75 and above   
 Nil 
 65 – 74 
 Rs. 100 
 50 – 64  
 Rs. 200 & will not be allowed for the current sitting 
  Below 50 
 To repeat the course 
 Students who absent themselves on the reopening day shall be fined at double the rate per day.
 No leave can be granted from the test unless for reasons of grave necessity. In case of illness, a proper medical certificate must be produced before the close of the test period.
 lf without leave or under any false pretext a student be absent from any test, he shall be treated as having obtained zero marks in the test.
 Procedure for OD: A student who participates in officially sanctioned academic/cultural/co-curricular/sports activities during the regular working days is eligible for leave as on Other Duty (OD). The procedure for applying for OD is as follows: The student before leaving the college on OD shall get the appropriate application form filled with the recommendation of the HOD/Coordinator/Convener/Director concerned and submit the same to the Vice-Principal. The application form shall clearly indicate the date of leaving the college and the date of rejoining of regular study back at the college. In return, he/she report to the vice-Principal and get his / her signature on the OD form to complete the process.
 Chronic absenteeism is considered as indiscipline. The Dean (P&A) will obtain periodic lists of such absentees from the departments and after scrutinizing by Discipline Committeesuch students will he removed from the roll

</header><div class="kingster-page-title-wrap  kingster-style-medium kingster-left-align" ><div class="kingster-header-transparent-substitute" ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-overlay"  ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-container kingster-container" ><div class="kingster-page-title-content kingster-item-pdlr"  ><h1 class="kingster-page-title"  >Attendance</h1></div></div></div>	<div class="kingster-page-wrapper" id="kingster-page-wrapper" ><div class="gdlr-core-page-builder-body clearfix"><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section-container gdlr-core-container clearfix" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column gdlr-core-column-60 gdlr-core-column-first" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column-content-margin gdlr-core-js "   ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column-content clearfix gdlr-core-js "   ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-element" ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item gdlr-core-item-pdlr gdlr-core-item-pdb gdlr-core-left-align"  ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item-content" style="text-transform: none ;"  ><ol>
<li style="text-align: justify;">Attendance will be marked at the beginning of each class.</li>
<li style="text-align: justify;">Students shall assemble in the respective lecture rooms before the second bell.</li>
<li style="text-align: justify;">In every class, each student shall have a specified seat and shall not occupy any other seat without the permission of the teacher.</li>
<li style="text-align: justify;">No student shall absent themselves from the College without obtaining leave except in case of sudden illness or ether circumstances which may prevent them from so doing. The Vice-Principal is the authority for granting leave.</li>
<li style="text-align: justify;">Application for leave must be written specifying clearly the reasons. They must be countersigned by the Parent or Guardian or Hall Warden before being sent to the Vice-Principal. Sick leave exceeding two days should be supported by a Medical Certificate.</li>
<li style="text-align: justify;">Students who absent themselves from College without leave shall pay a fine according to the following rule :<br />
<table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;" border="1">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 50%;"><strong> Attendance (%)    </strong></td>
<td style="width: 50%;"><strong>Fine</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 50%;">75 and above  </td>
<td style="width: 50%;">Nil</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 50%;">65 – 74</td>
<td style="width: 50%;">Rs. 100</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 50%;">50 – 64 </td>
<td style="width: 50%;">Rs. 200 & will not be allowed for the current sitting</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 50%;"> Below 50</td>
<td style="width: 50%;">To repeat the course</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</li>
<li>Students who absent themselves on the reopening day shall be fined at double the rate per day.</li>
<li>No leave can be granted from the test unless for reasons of grave necessity. In case of illness, a proper medical certificate must be produced before the close of the test period.</li>
<li>lf without leave or under any false pretext a student be absent from any test, he shall be treated as having obtained zero marks in the test.</li>
<li>Procedure for OD: A student who participates in officially sanctioned academic/cultural/co-curricular/sports activities during the regular working days is eligible for leave as on Other Duty (OD). The procedure for applying for OD is as follows: The student before leaving the college on OD shall get the appropriate application form filled with the recommendation of the HOD/Coordinator/Convener/Director concerned and submit the same to the Vice-Principal. The application form shall clearly indicate the date of leaving the college and the date of rejoining of regular study back at the college. In return, he/she report to the vice-Principal and get his / her signature on the OD form to complete the process.</li>
<li>Chronic absenteeism is considered as indiscipline. The Dean (P&A) will obtain periodic lists of such absentees from the departments and after scrutinizing by Discipline Committeesuch students will he removed from the roll</li>
</ol>

SLP – CHILD SUPPORT WORK IN ORPHANAGES
Attendance will be marked at the beginning of each class.
Students shall assemble in the respective lecture rooms before the second bell.
In every class, each student shall have a specified seat and shall not occupy any other seat without the permission of the teacher.

No student shall absent themselves from the College without obtaining leave except in case of sudden illness or ether circumstances which may prevent them from so doing. The Vice-Principal is the authority for granting leave.

Application for leave must be written specifying clearly the reasons. They must be countersigned by the Parent or Guardian or Hall Warden before being sent to the Vice-Principal. Sick leave exceeding two days should be supported by a Medical Certificate.

Students who absent themselves from College without leave shall pay a fine according to the following rule :  Attendance (%)     Fine 75 and above   Nil 65 – 74 Rs. 100 50 – 64  Rs. 200 & will not be allowed for the current sitting  Below 50 To repeat the course
Students who absent themselves on the reopening day shall be fined at double the rate per day.
No leave can be granted from the test unless for reasons of grave necessity. In case of illness, a proper medical certificate must be produced before the close of the test period.
lf without leave or under any false pretext a student be absent from any test, he shall be treated as having obtained zero marks in the test.

Procedure for OD: A student who participates in officially sanctioned academic/cultural/co-curricular/sports activities during the regular working days is eligible for leave as on Other Duty (OD). The procedure for applying for OD is as follows: The student before leaving the college on OD shall get the appropriate application form filled with the recommendation of the HOD/Coordinator/Convener/Director concerned and submit the same to the Vice-Principal. The application form shall clearly indicate the date of leaving the college and the date of rejoining of regular study back at the college. In return, he/she report to the vice-Principal and get his / her signature on the OD form to complete the process.

Chronic absenteeism is considered as indiscipline. The Dean (P&A) will obtain periodic lists of such absentees from the departments and after scrutinizing by Discipline Committeesuch students will he removed from the roll

 PLACEMENT CELL 
     The American College has been committed to excellence since its inception especially in terms of moulding the future of its students. The Placement Cell of The American College is committed to providing placement support to students matching their interest areas and academic profile and based on the demand from the external milieu.  The cell focuses on students especially the outgoing (final year students) from both under-graduate and post-graduate programmes of  aided and self-financed programmes. The placement Cell conducts placement related training and awareness programmes in the campus and organizes campus interviews and placement drives for the benefit of both aided and self-financed stream students.        
  
  Directors of Placement Cell: 
    Mr.S.Murali
    Dr. S.c.b. Samuel Anbu Selvan

<p style="font-weight: 400; text-align: justify;">    The American College has been committed to excellence since its inception especially in terms of moulding the future of its students. The Placement Cell of The American College is committed to providing placement support to students matching their interest areas and academic profile and based on the demand from the external milieu.  The cell focuses on students especially the outgoing (final year students) from both under-graduate and post-graduate programmes of  aided and self-financed programmes. The placement Cell conducts placement related training and awareness programmes in the campus and organizes campus interviews and placement drives for the benefit of both aided and self-financed stream students.        </p>

 JIVANA JYOTI – ITS BEGINNING AT MADURAI 
 The American College, further to its focus on academic excellence, is keen on reaching out to the needy persons and in creating equal opportunities in the society. Jivana Jyoti (Light for Life) is a programme that has been designed and run for the welfare of the physically challenged persons for the last 24 years.
 Jivana Jyoti at Madurai was started in the year 1990 with financial help from the Inter Church Service Association (ICSA) at Madras as the branch for the southern region of Jivana Jyoti, Madras. The Educational Development Services (EDS), India located in 93, Pantheon Road, Chennai under ICSA is in partnership with Jivana Jyoti at Madurai providing financial support every year. It is a partnership programme for training and rehabilitation of differently abled persons.
 A total of 412 persons (248 boys and 164 girls) from urban and rural Tamil Nadu have received training. The minimum qualification for entry into the course is a pass in higher secondary.
 In order to meet the growing and development needs, we are looking out for additional support from other sources for certain specific needs in the partnership programme.
 An endowment fund has been established with contributions from individuals and organization in the USA, which enabled grant of financial assistance to the needy students of Jivana Jyoti.
 Public recognition of the efforts for the differently abled has been encouraging to the college. In 1995 Lions Club, aura and the society for the physically handicapped honored Jivana Jyoti. In 1996-97 the city cultural association adjudged the training centre and the computer facilities as the best and gave an award of merit. The task now is to enlarge the programme to benefit more such persons.
 PHYSICAL PLAN OF THE COMPUTER CENTRE: 
 The computer center in the Department of Applied Science is designed for free and convenient mobility of the differently abled students. We have 50 computers in the department with one server. The server is a WINDOWS NT Environment, in which the softwares like C, C++, JAVA, .NET, DTP, FLASH, and Visual Basic have been installed for the training of the students. Students gain good knowledge as we provide them with exposure on the latest softwares in the field.
 The class room is located in the Department of Applied Science, next to the lab, in which 30 students can be seated. The need for a hostel was keenly felt to accommodate students who come from long distances especially when the nature and severity of the differently abled make travel almost impossible in public transport every day. A hostel was constructed in 1991 with financial aid from ICSA near the centre to accommodate 24 students (12 boys and 12 girls). The design and plan of the hostel are physically challenged friendly.
 Placement after training has been good and is improving. The private sector and the Government are the main employers. The following numbers have got employed in public and private sectors.
 Placements 
 FOUNDER & FIRST DIRECTOR 
 Dr. R.P. Riesz is an Emeritus Missionary of the United Church Board for World Ministries. He served in India from 1962 in The American College, Madurai and in Teaching institutions of the Church of South India. Dr. R. P. Riesz is a Physicist and Computer applications enthusiast. He is a First Director and Founder of the Jivana Jyoti in Madurai.
 His connection with India and a host of Indian Colleagues and Friends is intimate and detailed as is his acquaintance with the language, music and culture of South India. Now he is presently retired and living in Pleasant Hill, Tennessee.
 COURSE OBJECTIVES 
 At the end of the course a graduated student can:
 Be able to find a job
 Be able to run existing data entry software
 Be able to do secretarial tasks, including word processing (Letter writing etc.,)
 Be able to understand and use code files in several languages / packages (debugging/compiling/removing syntax errors)
 Be able to use spreadsheet/word processors for custom work.
 Understand the “Problem space” for a customer (estimate development time / requirements)
 Understand several common “problem spaces” (Accounting, Payroll, Inventory, Billing, Drafting, Word processing, DTP, Web designing, Data entry etc.,)
 Be able to connect up a computer system
 Recognize internal parts (Drives Chips, Cards, Power etc.,)
 Understand fundamental software structures in the computer (DOS, WINDOWS, system configuration)
 Exhibit self confidence : Have success-experience, job motivation (Spoken English Interview skills etc.,)
 Read and understand technical material in English (Books, magazines, manual etc.,)
 Maintain document on any computer job
 Be “Officially” prepared for job.
 The Diploma is awarded by the American College. As per the instructions given by the VRC, the syllabus was revised

    width: 400px !important;
    height: 160px;
    border: 1px solid #ccc;
    overflow: hidden;
    padding: 10px;
    position: relative;
}

.cstm-news-scroll {
    position: absolute;

    animation: scrollUp 20s linear infinite;

<p>Dr.D.Rachel Malini</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>JIVANA JYOTI – ITS BEGINNING AT MADURAI</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The American College, further to its focus on academic excellence, is keen on reaching out to the needy persons and in creating equal opportunities in the society. Jivana Jyoti (Light for Life) is a programme that has been designed and run for the welfare of the physically challenged persons for the last 24 years.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Jivana Jyoti at Madurai was started in the year 1990 with financial help from the Inter Church Service Association (ICSA) at Madras as the branch for the southern region of Jivana Jyoti, Madras. The Educational Development Services (EDS), India located in 93, Pantheon Road, Chennai under ICSA is in partnership with Jivana Jyoti at Madurai providing financial support every year. It is a partnership programme for training and rehabilitation of differently abled persons.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">A total of 412 persons (248 boys and 164 girls) from urban and rural Tamil Nadu have received training. The minimum qualification for entry into the course is a pass in higher secondary.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">In order to meet the growing and development needs, we are looking out for additional support from other sources for certain specific needs in the partnership programme.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">An endowment fund has been established with contributions from individuals and organization in the USA, which enabled grant of financial assistance to the needy students of Jivana Jyoti.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Public recognition of the efforts for the differently abled has been encouraging to the college. In 1995 Lions Club, aura and the society for the physically handicapped honored Jivana Jyoti. In 1996-97 the city cultural association adjudged the training centre and the computer facilities as the best and gave an award of merit. The task now is to enlarge the programme to benefit more such persons.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>PHYSICAL PLAN OF THE COMPUTER CENTRE:</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The computer center in the Department of Applied Science is designed for free and convenient mobility of the differently abled students. We have 50 computers in the department with one server. The server is a WINDOWS NT Environment, in which the softwares like C, C++, JAVA, .NET, DTP, FLASH, and Visual Basic have been installed for the training of the students. Students gain good knowledge as we provide them with exposure on the latest softwares in the field.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The class room is located in the Department of Applied Science, next to the lab, in which 30 students can be seated. The need for a hostel was keenly felt to accommodate students who come from long distances especially when the nature and severity of the differently abled make travel almost impossible in public transport every day. A hostel was constructed in 1991 with financial aid from ICSA near the centre to accommodate 24 students (12 boys and 12 girls). The design and plan of the hostel are physically challenged friendly.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Placement after training has been good and is improving. The private sector and the Government are the main employers. The following numbers have got employed in public and private sectors.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong><a href="https://americancollege.edu.in/amc-storage/2015/06/Placements.pdf">Placements</a></strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>FOUNDER & FIRST DIRECTOR</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Dr. R.P. Riesz is an Emeritus Missionary of the United Church Board for World Ministries. He served in India from 1962 in The American College, Madurai and in Teaching institutions of the Church of South India. Dr. R. P. Riesz is a Physicist and Computer applications enthusiast. He is a First Director and Founder of the Jivana Jyoti in Madurai.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">His connection with India and a host of Indian Colleagues and Friends is intimate and detailed as is his acquaintance with the language, music and culture of South India. Now he is presently retired and living in Pleasant Hill, Tennessee.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>COURSE OBJECTIVES</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">At the end of the course a graduated student can:</p>
<ul style="text-align: justify;">
<li>Be able to find a job</li>
<li>Be able to run existing data entry software</li>
<li>Be able to do secretarial tasks, including word processing (Letter writing etc.,)</li>
<li>Be able to understand and use code files in several languages / packages (debugging/compiling/removing syntax errors)</li>
<li>Be able to use spreadsheet/word processors for custom work.</li>
<li>Understand the “Problem space” for a customer (estimate development time / requirements)</li>
<li>Understand several common “problem spaces” (Accounting, Payroll, Inventory, Billing, Drafting, Word processing, DTP, Web designing, Data entry etc.,)</li>
<li>Be able to connect up a computer system</li>
<li>Recognize internal parts (Drives Chips, Cards, Power etc.,)</li>
<li>Understand fundamental software structures in the computer (DOS, WINDOWS, system configuration)</li>
<li>Exhibit self confidence : Have success-experience, job motivation (Spoken English Interview skills etc.,)</li>
<li>Read and understand technical material in English (Books, magazines, manual etc.,)</li>
<li>Maintain document on any computer job</li>
<li>Be “Officially” prepared for job.</li>
</ul>

SLP – CHILD SUPPORT WORK IN ORPHANAGES
Be able to find a job
Be able to run existing data entry software
Be able to do secretarial tasks, including word processing (Letter writing etc.,)
Be able to understand and use code files in several languages / packages (debugging/compiling/removing syntax errors)
Be able to use spreadsheet/word processors for custom work.
Understand the “Problem space” for a customer (estimate development time / requirements)
Understand several common “problem spaces” (Accounting, Payroll, Inventory, Billing, Drafting, Word processing, DTP, Web designing, Data entry etc.,)
Be able to connect up a computer system
Recognize internal parts (Drives Chips, Cards, Power etc.,)
Understand fundamental software structures in the computer (DOS, WINDOWS, system configuration)
Exhibit self confidence : Have success-experience, job motivation (Spoken English Interview skills etc.,)
Read and understand technical material in English (Books, magazines, manual etc.,)
Maintain document on any computer job

 Department of Applied Science 
 HISTORY 
 In 1978 The American College formally opened the Department of Applied Science. This is an innovative, non-teaching Department of the college. It is designed to use the rich resources of College Staff and facilities in the service of the college itself and the community around it. The Department of Applied Science manages many of the technical facilities of the College, such as the computer centre, for the benefit and use of the entire College.
 In 1982 the D.A.S. started the Computer Centre providing computer training for the college students and night time extension courses for outsiders.
 INFRASTRUCTURE AND FACILITIES 
 In 1978 The American College opened the Department of Applied Science which is designed to use the rich resources of College Staff and the facilities in the service of the college itself and the community around it. In 1982 the D.A.S. started the Computer Centre providing computer training for the college students and night time extension courses for those who applied for it.
 The Centre is equipped with 25 Nos. PIV and PIII IBM PC. The System has 256MB, 128 MB Main memory, 80 GB and 40 GB Hard Disk Drive and 1.44 Floppy Drive with 14 inch color Monitors. The Centre has three 3 KVA UPS with 2 hours backup. In view of the unpredictable nature of power supply, all the systems can run through Uninterrupted Power Supplies (UPS). Laser and dot matrix printers are in the centre. The provisions for on line teaching are also available.
 The Center has all major language compliers like C, Fortran ,Pascal, C++, Basic, Java, C# and the major software packages like FoxPro, MS-OFFICE, Corel Draw, Page Maker, Photo Shop, Windows, Oracle 9i, Visual Studio, Flash, Tally 9 etc .
 In December 2006, DAS took charge of maintaining the Central Instrumentation Centre (CIC). Instruments like X-ray unit for crystallographic studies, 3 types of Lathe, High temperature furnace and a Scanning Electron microscope are in CIC center.
 The Documentation Centre has a Photo copier (Canon) machine which is fully utilized by the college and students.
 Department of Applied Science, The American College collaborated with Tally India Pvt. Ltd., and started Tally Graduate Program since February 2007 for college and Jivana Jyoti students. This is a regular tie up with commerce department.
 The Department of Applied Science has another phase of work like Jivana Jyoti (Light of life), is a program to bring light into the lives of the Physically challenged since 1990, and it arose out of the American College’s concern for this section of society. It trains the physically disabled in various computer skills and functional English for a year and to make them employable, self reliant and socially productive. It is in collaboration with the Educational and Development services of (India) Madras from 1990 that this project was started. In 1992 a specially designed hostel with facilities like furniture , library, recreation systems and indoor games for physically disabled was built to accommodate girls and boys.

 Volume 3

 Processing of transactions involving VAT
 Generation and printing of VAT computation and VAT forms
 Enabling TDS and Service Tax features
 Setting up master for TDS and Service Tax
 Generating and printing of TDS and Service Tax reports
 Processing of transactions involving TDS and Service Tax.
 Fee Structure 
 Tuition Fees: Rs.3250.00/- (72 Hrs. course)
 Admission Process 
 Any students of our college can join in this course.
 Academic Programs 
 DAS continues to support the academic programs of the college BCA, B.Sc., computer science, B.Sc., Physics, chemistry, M.Sc., programs and Jivana Jyoti courses by providing computer facilities for the students.
 M.A. and M.Phil., (Economics) students were trained in Statistical Software called SPSS.
 Indira Gandhi National University and PGDCA practical sessions are conducted in the computer centre.
 Certificate and Diploma courses in computer applications and computer languages are also offered to the students of various department of the college.

</header><div class="kingster-page-title-wrap  kingster-style-medium kingster-left-align" ><div class="kingster-header-transparent-substitute" ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-overlay"  ></div><div class="kingster-page-title-container kingster-container" ><div class="kingster-page-title-content kingster-item-pdlr"  ><h1 class="kingster-page-title"  >Department of Applied Science</h1></div></div></div>	<div class="kingster-page-wrapper" id="kingster-page-wrapper" ><div class="gdlr-core-page-builder-body clearfix"><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-section-container gdlr-core-container clearfix" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column gdlr-core-column-60 gdlr-core-column-first" ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column-content-margin gdlr-core-js "   ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-column-content clearfix gdlr-core-js "   ><div class="gdlr-core-pbf-element" ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item gdlr-core-item-pdlr gdlr-core-item-pdb gdlr-core-left-align"  ><div class="gdlr-core-text-box-item-content" style="text-transform: none ;"  ><p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>HISTORY</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">In 1978 The American College formally opened the Department of Applied Science. This is an innovative, non-teaching Department of the college. It is designed to use the rich resources of College Staff and facilities in the service of the college itself and the community around it. The Department of Applied Science manages many of the technical facilities of the College, such as the computer centre, for the benefit and use of the entire College.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">In 1982 the D.A.S. started the Computer Centre providing computer training for the college students and night time extension courses for outsiders.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>INFRASTRUCTURE AND FACILITIES</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">In 1978 The American College opened the Department of Applied Science which is designed to use the rich resources of College Staff and the facilities in the service of the college itself and the community around it. In 1982 the D.A.S. started the Computer Centre providing computer training for the college students and night time extension courses for those who applied for it.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The Centre is equipped with 25 Nos. PIV and PIII IBM PC. The System has 256MB, 128 MB Main memory, 80 GB and 40 GB Hard Disk Drive and 1.44 Floppy Drive with 14 inch color Monitors. The Centre has three 3 KVA UPS with 2 hours backup. In view of the unpredictable nature of power supply, all the systems can run through Uninterrupted Power Supplies (UPS). Laser and dot matrix printers are in the centre. The provisions for on line teaching are also available.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The Center has all major language compliers like C, Fortran ,Pascal, C++, Basic, Java, C# and the major software packages like FoxPro, MS-OFFICE, Corel Draw, Page Maker, Photo Shop, Windows, Oracle 9i, Visual Studio, Flash, Tally 9 etc .</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">In December 2006, DAS took charge of maintaining the Central Instrumentation Centre (CIC). Instruments like X-ray unit for crystallographic studies, 3 types of Lathe, High temperature furnace and a Scanning Electron microscope are in CIC center.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The Documentation Centre has a Photo copier (Canon) machine which is fully utilized by the college and students.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Department of Applied Science, The American College collaborated with Tally India Pvt. Ltd., and started Tally Graduate Program since February 2007 for college and Jivana Jyoti students. This is a regular tie up with commerce department.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The Department of Applied Science has another phase of work like Jivana Jyoti (Light of life), is a program to bring light into the lives of the Physically challenged since 1990, and it arose out of the American College’s concern for this section of society. It trains the physically disabled in various computer skills and functional English for a year and to make them employable, self reliant and socially productive. It is in collaboration with the Educational and Development services of (India) Madras from 1990 that this project was started. In 1992 a specially designed hostel with facilities like furniture , library, recreation systems and indoor games for physically disabled was built to accommodate girls and boys.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Tally Graduate Program</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Course Details</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Volume 1</strong></p>
<ul style="text-align: justify;">
<li>The basic Tally features</li>
<li>Description of main features and components of Tally.</li>
<li>Creation and Maintenance of company information required by Tally</li>
<li>Basic features of Tally Accounting system</li>
<li>Basic features of Tally Inventory system</li>
</ul>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Volume 2</strong></p>
<ul style="text-align: justify;">
<li>Advanced features of Tally</li>
<li>Maintenance of bill and Invoice details and tracking receivable and payables Creation and Maintenance of cost centers</li>
<li>Creation and Maintenance of multiple currencies</li>
<li>Creation and maintenance of stock go downs and stock points</li>
<li>Creation and maintenance of budget and scenarios</li>
<li>Performing interest calculations</li>
<li>Generating and printing of information statements</li>
<li>System administration and house keeping features</li>
</ul>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Volume 3</strong></p>
<ul style="text-align: justify;">
<li>Creation of a company enabling VAT features</li>
<li>Processing of transactions involving VAT</li>
<li>Generation and printing of VAT computation and VAT forms</li>
<li>Enabling TDS and Service Tax features</li>
<li>Setting up master for TDS and Service Tax</li>
<li>Generating and printing of TDS and Service Tax reports</li>
<li>Processing of transactions involving TDS and Service Tax.</li>
</ul>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Fee Structure</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Tuition Fees: Rs.3250.00/- (72 Hrs. course)</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Admission Process</strong></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Any students of our college can join in this course.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><strong>Academic Programs</strong></p>
<ul style="text-align: justify;">
<li>DAS continues to support the academic programs of the college BCA, B.Sc., computer science, B.Sc., Physics, chemistry, M.Sc., programs and Jivana Jyoti courses by providing computer facilities for the students.</li>
<li>M.A. and M.Phil., (Economics) students were trained in Statistical Software called SPSS.</li>
<li>Indira Gandhi National University and PGDCA practical sessions are conducted in the computer centre.</li>
<li>Certificate and Diploma courses in computer applications and computer languages are also offered to the students of various department of the college.</li>
</ul>
<p style="text-align: justify;"> </p>

 STUDY CENTRE FOR INDIAN LITERATURE IN ENGLISH AND TRANSLATION 
 Study Centre for Indian Literature in English and Translation, better known by its acronym, SCILET was established in 1985. SCILET has since that time steadily developed its own identity in terms of its objectives, its library and associated facilities and its many related programmes. 
 SCILET is basically a research library with more than 10,000 volumes of literature written by resident or expatriate Indians in English medium, or translated into English from Indian languages.

<p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="color: #000000;">Study Centre for Indian Literature in English and Translation, better known by its acronym, SCILET was established in 1985. SCILET has since that time steadily developed its own identity in terms of its objectives, its library and associated facilities and its many related programmes.</span></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="color: #000000;"> SCILET is basically a research library with more than 10,000 volumes of literature written by resident or expatriate Indians in English medium, or translated into English from Indian languages.</span></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="color: #000000;"> To know more about SCILET click the link below: <a style="color: #000000;" href="http://www.scilet.in/">SCILET</a></span></p>

    position: absolute;

 Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) 
 The American College, since its inception, has been adopting a series of changes in its curriculum matching with the advancements in the various Academic subject areas, and the emerging needs and demands from the society. The global perspective of the college has also been a driving force to provide quality education to its students. Autonomy has provided a platform for each department to have their own departmental objectives leading to the emergence of scholars with interdisciplinary background.
 Intellectual profundity and wider choices characterize liberal arts and science undergraduate education. CBCS allows students to cross the artificial boundaries of varied academic disciplines and enables them to get the insights of several disciplines bringing out the inherent interest and aptitude.
 After two-years of deliberations, our faculty has brought out a version of the choice based credit system that suits the needs and aspirations of the American college community. It is not just a change in the nomenclature but also a paradigm shift in the education practices.
 The following are also some of the other expected outcomes:
 CBCS will develop human resources to suit a wide range of career opportunities
 It will promote inter-departmental cooperation within the college for a better utilization of the existing infrastructure and human resources.
 The students can go beyond institutional boundaries by way of transferring credits across accredited institutions.

 Policy: 
 Being a college with a difference since its inception in 1881, the American College, Madurai has been an academia par excellence in serving the cause of Higher Education imbued with a holistic perspective in imparting the state-of-the-art knowledge and skills with high seriousness and robustness relevant to contemporary times. Pedagogy of the Twenty First Century – updated and innovative- with a right blend of cutting-edge research has been the hallmark of the college. Fair subscription to original ideas, and framing curriculum adopting novel strategies, improvisations in Teaching- Learning process and evaluation patterns for an effective pedagogy and knowledge-generation/transmission through village outreach programmes, extension projects and  competency- building workshops through the munificent grants offered by the Research and Development Committee of the college have always accelerated the growth of the institution.
 In tune with the recommendations of the Kothari commission on National Policy on Education (1968), the college had championed the cause of Higher Education with three cardinal principles of Excellence, Relevance and Employability . Catering to the needs of the students through enhanced teacher- responsibility coupled with teaching-learning strategies in the stated domains, the college has always addressed the needs and priorities of its stakeholders through consultations and perfect professional expertise at various levels. The spirit of inquiry and conscientious subscription to fair functioning have led to the active research slant in all these approaches. The erstwhile office of the Academic Dean and an exclusive office of Dean for Curriculum Development and Research later, with the advice of the Research and Development committee, have been engaged in monitoring and encouraging the progress of research of the faculty and students.
 In this post-second cycle of NAAC, research policies were revamped and newer references were created to strengthen the domain-centered approach. This in turn, has enhanced infrastructure and research equipment of the departments many fold. The college has made a paradigm shift in creating common instrumentation facilities that offer channels for pursuing innovations and improvisations so as to create a fresh ambience and eco systems for multi-disciplinary and cross-major learning and research. Today, as an integral part of the curriculum, the college promotes independent and group investigations and dissertation studies among undergraduate and postgraduate students. It also encourages its faculty to handle projects that would act as catalysts for developing grant proposals to attract funding agencies in India and abroad.
 Positioned on firm foundation and backed by a century-old experience, the research policy of the college articulates that quality research, which engenders a sound knowledge-based society, is the hallmark of learning in the portal of Higher Education in India. Through effective and innovative measures, the research facility available in the college will direct, augment and invigorate a spirit of enquiry, scientific temperament, research aptitude, capacity-building, and character-formation in grooming researchers. These ideals are well envisioned and nurtured by the object of the institution.
 Practice: 
 Induction and duties of Research scholars: 
 Interested scholars shall apply to the respective universities to clear the eligibility test conducted in July and February.
 Scholars shall apply for research position exist in the college and appear for counseling at the beginning of the academic calendar and the provisional order of admission will be issued by the Principal
 Scholars shall meet the Dean of Research and the original certificates will be submitted in the office.
 On completion of formalities the scholar will be issued a Roll No like 20 PHD **, 20 PHD MAT ** and an ID card which shall be worn by the scholar inside the premises
 An orientation program will be arranged for the newly enrolled scholars.
 A separate attendance register to be maintained at Principals office for all the scholars
 Leave applications to be submitted to the principal’s office forwarded by the Guide on a regular basis
 On-duty leave shall be availed on outside works/conferences /workshops etc.
 Maternity leave is allowed as per UGC norms.
 A Research Advisory Committee for each Department (RAC) is to be formed and the same will finalize the study design and methodology of the research to be done.
 RAC shall comprise: Principal, Dean of research, Heads, Research Guides of the department. (Optional – Two technical experts may be added to the committee for reviewing the progress of the scholars)
 Subsequently scholar will be assigned a mentor for selecting a research TOPIC/GUIDE
 Eligible scholars will be paid a scholarship each month as decided by the administration.
 Scholars shall pay a nominal fee every year for the college and also the University as per requirements.
 Should complete the course work in the first semester. As per MKU rules COE will conduct examinations in regard to the course works.
 The course works shall have 2/4 different courses as prescribed by MKU in the circular no. MKU/PhD/CW2016/Circular-AC to earn 12/14 credits.

 Attendance 
 Attendance will be marked at the beginning of each class.
 Students shall assemble in the respective lecture rooms before the second bell.
 In every class, each student shall have a specified seat and shall not occupy any other seat without the permission of the teacher.
 No student shall absent themselves from the College without obtaining leave except in case of sudden illness or ether circumstances which may prevent them from so doing. The Vice-Principal is the authority for granting leave.
 Application for leave must be written specifying clearly the reasons. They must be countersigned by the Parent or Guardian or Hall Warden before being sent to the Vice-Principal. Sick leave exceeding two days should be supported by a Medical Certificate.
 Students who absent themselves from College without leave shall pay a fine according to the following rule :

 To repeat the course 
 Students who absent themselves on the reopening day shall be fined at double the rate per day.
 No leave can be granted from the test unless for reasons of grave necessity. In case of illness, a proper medical certificate must be produced before the close of the test period.
 lf without leave or under any false pretext a student be absent from any test, he shall be treated as having obtained zero marks in the test.
 Procedure for OD: A student who participates in officially sanctioned academic/cultural/co-curricular/sports activities during the regular working days is eligible for leave as on Other Duty (OD). The procedure for applying for OD is as follows: The student before leaving the college on OD shall get the appropriate application form filled with the recommendation of the HOD/Coordinator/Convener/Director concerned and submit the same to the Vice-Principal. The application form shall clearly indicate the date of leaving the college and the date of rejoining of regular study back at the college. In return, he/she report to the vice-Principal and get his / her signature on the OD form to complete the process.
 Chronic absenteeism is considered as indiscipline. The Dean (P&A) will obtain periodic lists of such absentees from the departments and after scrutinizing by Discipline Committeesuch students will he removed from the roll
